title: Add privacy-safe EngineeringException classification for OLQ failures
goal: Diagnose the remaining RetrieveWithUpgrade EngineeringTargetInvocationException without changing migration behavior or publishing arbitrary Siemens exception text, by deriving bounded semantic tags and deterministic text fingerprints from the official EngineeringException MessageData/DetailMessageData surfaces.
scope: Coding-agent candidate scope is exactly src/TiaV21Worker/Program.cs unless a tiny source-level test file is strictly necessary. Do not modify workflows, other tasks, bootstrap scripts, generator/domain/compiler semantics, runner configuration, secrets, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

Preserve the exact qualification sequence and behavior: RetrieveWithUpgrade -> Save -> Archive -> current-version Retrieve verification. Do not add fallback APIs, retries, alternate OpenMode, UI/headless changes, migration workarounds, or exception swallowing.

For caught Siemens.Engineering.EngineeringException instances, inspect MessageData.Text and DetailMessageData only in memory and derive public-safe diagnostics. Never copy arbitrary MessageData/DetailMessageData text into QualificationResult.Failure, console output, uploaded artifacts, issue comments, or other public evidence.

Append to the existing public-safe failure token a deterministic bounded diagnostic suffix containing: zero or more tags from the fixed allowlist, detail-count, a SHA-256 fingerprint of MessageData.Text when present, and a SHA-256 aggregate fingerprint of DetailMessageData.Text values when present. Fingerprints may be truncated only if the truncation length is fixed and at least 16 hexadecimal characters.

The only allowed public semantic tag labels are: missing-product, unreleased-content, unsupported-version, invalid-archive, access-denied, user-abort, target-conflict, license-missing, unknown. No source/library/type/product names or arbitrary words may appear in the public suffix.

Tag derivation must be deterministic from case-insensitive matching of the in-memory Siemens text. Use conservative phrase/term checks for the fixed categories; when no category matches, emit unknown. Multiple matching safe tags may be emitted in a stable deterministic order.

Preserve full Exception.ToString() only in the existing runner-local QualificationResult.FailureDetails exactly as today; do not broaden its publication. Preserve current phase/type/HRESULT tokens unchanged as the prefix of Failure.

The classification must be null-safe for absent MessageData or DetailMessageData and must not turn diagnostic-access failures into qualification success or a new migration failure. If safe diagnostic extraction itself cannot be completed, preserve the original phase/type/HRESULT failure token and optionally append only unknown.
Candidate/unmerged worker code must never execute on the trusted Windows/TIA runner. Windows/TIA validation is post-merge trusted-main only.

requirements: Candidate diff stays within src/TiaV21Worker/Program.cs plus at most one strictly bounded source-level test if justified; no protected infrastructure changes.
RetrieveWithUpgrade, Save, Archive, close, native Retrieve and success/failure semantics are unchanged.
Existing public failure prefix remains exactly phase:<token> type:<ExceptionType> hresult:0xXXXXXXXX.

For EngineeringException failures, the suffix exposes only fixed allowlist tags, detail-count, and deterministic SHA-256 fingerprints; arbitrary Siemens MessageData/DetailMessageData text is never public.
Tag output order and fingerprint construction are deterministic; absent/no-match data is handled safely and yields unknown rather than raw text.
FailureDetails continues to retain full raw exception information only in the runner-local manifest and the trusted public workflow remains unchanged.
Qualification identity, source/output hashes, archive naming, existing-archive conflict behavior, whitelist synchronization and TIA connection ordering remain unchanged.
Linux deterministic CI remains green and no candidate Windows/TIA execution occurs.
Primary connected ChatGPT performs independent exact-SHA CODE_REVIEW because the candidate is authored by the coding agent.
tia: After independent review and trusted merge, run /run-olq-001 from issue #19 on trusted main without changing registry ACLs or runner configuration.
If RetrieveWithUpgrade still fails, public evidence must retain phase/type/HRESULT and additionally provide only the bounded safe tags/detail-count/fingerprints needed for the next diagnosis.
No arbitrary Siemens exception text, absolute paths, usernames, vendor payload content or library object names may appear in public evidence.
A PASS still requires the unchanged OLQ-001 qualification gates; this diagnostic task does not claim to fix migration.
